entries.text: The tracker now names Ask The Recruiter Research as the publisher of its dataset and links to its sources.
Public tracker data requests and downloads ask you to wait when request limits are reached.
Chart embeds include a link to the free resume match check.
Use resume in the tracker email match actions.
Clicks on the free match check links are now counted, so we can see which tracker pages send people to Ask The Recruiter.
The follow star and employer names on update cards are large enough to tap, and the weekly chart and totals table can be scrolled with a keyboard.
The tracker home page now ends with a dated "Key numbers" block: the same quotable figures, with their date, that the tracker publishes for AI search tools, plus how to cite them.
Company, country and industry pages now link to the same company, country or sector in our layoff tracker, where both trackers have a page for it.

Every sign-up link on the hiring tracker, including the site header's, now carries one tracker tag, and the company-card buttons go to the free resume match check. The site menu's script loads again on every sub-page, and a brief database error while filtering quickly is retried instead of shown.
Company and places pages now show the free resume check link near the top, under the heading; the existing links further down stay.
The tracker now has its own llms.txt with dated, sourced figures, and phones get a closable bar linking to the free resume check.

Clicking filters quickly no longer makes the tracker's data requests fail: rapid clicks are combined into one request with your final filters, and the server computes each uncached view once at a time, with a short automatic retry instead of an error when it is busy.
Company pages for employers whose name is in a non-Latin script open again instead of showing a not-found page.
Every virtual route (places, roles, recall, corrections, press, methodology, update log, sources, every place page) now carries the tracked sign-up line, not only the dashboard and company pages.
UTM-tagged sign-up line on the tracker page and company pages.
Methodology page and update log of this tracker's own.
